lines.text: When using the wood it needs to be completely dried out and
free of any cracks or rot.
Mao jue is the primary component of a scaffolding
structure. It maintains at least a 70 mm nominal
external diameter.
Kao jue are at least 45 mm in their
external diameter.
The grid panel
is the basis of the
bamboo scaffolding;
the cantonese technical
term for the vertical pole
of a grid is pronounced as
“zam” (needle), and “hin” for the
horizontal pole, and lastly “cheong”
for the diagonal pole.
Scaffolders do not need to work with a physi-
cal construction drawing in hand.
“using the heart as the drawing, using
the eyes as the ruler”
Scaffolders guide themselves completely by experience, and
adapt each project to the scaffolding site.
Bamboo scaffolding ex-
tends beyond the building
façade, occupying the space
between construction sites and
everyday urban life. Double-layered
scaffolds support workers along exteri-
or walls, while truss-out scaffolds extend
from buildings where ground-supported
structures are impractical. Protective canopies
and catch fans help intercept falling materials
above pedestrian routes.
Wrapped around these structures, green construction
nets form another protective layer, containing debris and
dust, providing shade, and moderating exposure to wind and
weather. Their presence changes not only the working conditions
inside the scaffold but also the appearance of the surrounding
streetscape. The familiar green covering temporarily transforms
buildings under construction into recognizable surfaces within the city,
making the boundary between active work and public space both functional
and visible.
The choice of green may also contribute to visual comfort, but this needs to be
distinguished from the net's documented safety functions. Green is often associated
with nature and visual calm; however, that association alone does not establish that
green construction nets are specifically designed to improve eye health or that their color
is prescribed to distinguish construction sites from surrounding buildings.
